planting.note: Plant bulbs, or divisions taken 'in the green' just after flowering, in fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Titania is one of the Greatorex double snowdrops bred in Norfolk in the mid-20th century and named, like its siblings, for a Shakespearean character.

directions: Plant bulbs 3 to 4 inches deep in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade beneath deciduous trees or shrubs. Titania is one of the Greatorex double snowdrops, bred in Norfolk, England by Heyrick Greatorex in the mid-20th century by crossing Galanthus nivalis f. pleniflorus with Galanthus plicatus, and like the rest of the series it carries the name of a Shakespearean heroine. The flower packs an extra ruff of inner segments inside the usual three outer petals, giving a fuller, rounder look than a single snowdrop. It is best grown alongside other Greatorex doubles and early woodland bulbs; lift and divide congested clumps in the green immediately after flowering for reliable establishment.

planting.note: Plant bulbs, or divisions taken 'in the green' just after flowering, in fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Lavinia is another of Heyrick Greatorex's Shakespeare-named double snowdrops from Norfolk.

directions: Plant bulbs 3 to 4 inches deep in evenly moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade beneath deciduous trees or shrubs. Lavinia is one of the Greatorex double snowdrops raised by Heyrick Greatorex in Norfolk, England, in the mid-20th century, part of a set of doubles he named for Shakespearean women. Each flower carries a tightly packed inner rosette of extra segments within the standard outer three petals. It increases steadily once established and is best grown in a shaded woodland or border setting alongside other named doubles; divide crowded clumps in the green right after flowering.

planting.note: Plant bulbs, or divisions taken 'in the green' just after flowering, in fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Desdemona is another of the Greatorex double snowdrops bred in Norfolk and named for an Othello character.

directions: Plant bulbs 3 to 4 inches deep in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade beneath deciduous trees or shrubs. Desdemona is one of Heyrick Greatorex's mid-20th-century Norfolk-bred double snowdrops, part of the Shakespeare-themed series that also includes Hippolyta, Jaquenetta, and Ophelia, distinguished by a fully double, tightly packed inner segment cluster. It is a dependable, moderately vigorous grower suited to a shaded border or woodland planting with other early bulbs and hellebores. Lift and divide congested clumps in the green just after flowering for the best transplant results.

planting.note: Plant bulbs 4-5 inches deep in fall in lean, gritty, sharply drained soil in full sun; this dwarf species tulip from the Tian Shan mountains of Central Asia needs a hot, dry summer dormancy to persist as a perennial.

directions: Tulipa vvedenskyi is a dwarf species tulip native to rocky slopes of the Tian Shan range in Central Asia, producing unusually large, broad, brilliant orange-red to scarlet flowers relative to its short stature, often with a darker basal blotch, over low tufts of wavy-margined gray-green leaves. It needs lean, sharply drained soil and a hot, dry summer dormancy to persist season after season, making it best suited to a rock garden, raised bed, or gravel planting rather than a regularly irrigated border. The species has also supplied breeding stock for some modern early-blooming dwarf tulip hybrids. Left undisturbed in suitable conditions it slowly builds into a long-lived clump rather than dwindling after a year or two like many border hybrid tulips.
